solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arrest and book holy man to appear in criminal court

indicators.note: the book and holy man are made to appear inside the reworked court, so these words place one piece within another
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of court are bent into a new order

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is a holy man

explanation.surface: A police arrest followed by charges and a holy man in the dock at a criminal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrest' looks like the police action, but it means to block; 'criminal' gives the shuffled ORUCT, opened after its first letter by 'to appear in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest progress is to block or impede it, a synonym sense of halting rather than detaining.

clue.text: Joke about Sidney being able to score

indicators.note: the joke is placed around Sidney's short name, so about here means surrounding

parts.note: a joke can be called 'one', as in 'have you heard the one about...'
SID is the usual short form of the name Sidney

explanation.surface: Someone tells a joke about a man called Sidney who can score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joke about Sidney' reads like a story's subject, but 'one' (as in 'heard the one about') wraps SID.
explanation.definitionFit: In football or rugby a player not offside is in a legal position and may score.

clue.text: They may be stirred but not shaken or drawn but not quartered

definitions.text: They may be stirred but not shaken or drawn but not quartered

parts.words: They may be stirred but not shaken or drawn but not quartered
parts.note: the phrases echo Bond's martini and the old 'hanged, drawn and quartered'

explanation.surface: A riddle mixing a Bond cocktail order with the old execution sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the wooden stumps are pulled up (drawn) at the end of a day's play; 'stir your stumps' is British slang for hurry up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's wicket uprights are pulled at close of play and figure in the idiom for getting moving.

clue.text: Wash out revolt in North? On the contrary

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, but which way round is then reversed
this says the stated containment is the other way about: the north letter goes inside the revolt, not the revolt inside it

parts.note: to rise up is to revolt, so a rise is a revolt
N is the compass abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: An instruction to wash something out, then a remark about a revolt in the North.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, RISE goes in N, which is impossible; 'On the contrary' flips it so N goes inside RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash out a cup is to swill it with clean water, a close synonym.

clue.text: Big ones are usually high in rank — or even high and rank

definitions.text: Big ones are usually high in rank — or even high and rank

parts.words: Big ones are usually high in rank — or even high and rank
parts.note: a 'big cheese' is an important person, high in rank; ripe dairy products can also be high (strong-smelling) and rank (smelly)

explanation.surface: A wry remark that important people are high-ranking and perhaps also smelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' and 'rank' turn from status words into words for a strong smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Big shots are called big ones of this kind, and strong varieties of the dairy food can reek.

clue.text: If blue this cannot be finally seen, but it can be seen if it has extremes of colour

definitions.text: If blue this cannot be finally seen

indicators.note: the word seen is said to hold something, so these words place the colour's ends inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A puzzling riddle about something blue that cannot be seen in the end, though it can be seen with colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of colour' gives C and R, which 'if it has' sets inside SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: In film effects a blue backdrop is replaced by other images, so it never appears in the finished shot.

clue.text: It projects game in university

parts.note: a cam is a projecting part on a rotating shaft
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Something sticks out of a game being played at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It projects' sounds like a film projector, but it is a cam, the machine part that sticks out from a shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the two ancient English seats of learning, the other being Oxford.

clue.text: All the team play once

definitions.meaning: every player on the side, each and every one of them
a fifteenth-century English morality play of that title, so a play of former times

explanation.surface: Every member of the side once took part in the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Two words split as 'every man' cover the whole team; joined they name a medieval morality drama.

clue.text: To provoke saints is unnecessary

parts.note: to needle someone is to provoke or irritate them

explanation.surface: Annoying holy people is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncalled for is without need, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Square one is in under 'blue'

parts.note: SQ is the abbreviation for square

indicators.note: the single letter for one is placed inside the word under

parts.note: taken as written
A means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: A cryptic sentence about square one being under a colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' is the slang verb meaning to spend money recklessly, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow cash is to waste it, the old slang sense of spending it freely.

clue.text: In the morning father gets measurement of current

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon
PERE is French for father

explanation.surface: Dad checks the electricity at breakfast time.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the SI unit used to measure electric current flow.

clue.text: Old blade makes further remarks to be heard

indicators.note: the remark word is to be heard rather than read, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: someone who adds is making further remarks

explanation.surface: An old blade speaks up with extra comments.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient cutting tool with an arched blade at right angles to the handle, used for shaping wood.

clue.text: Key gets this body of journalists into act

indicators.note: the journalists are put into the act, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an act
the press is the collective term for journalists

explanation.surface: A keyboard key is pushed while reporters burst into a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' does double duty: what a key undergoes when pushed, and the clue's pointer to the press.
explanation.definitionFit: A key on a keyboard is pushed down when used, so it is pressed down.

clue.text: Magnificent couple of boys

parts.note: Roy is a boy's name
Al is another boy's name

explanation.surface: Two lads are described as splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal and splendid, fit for a monarch, a synonym of grand.

clue.text: One's twice in the Blue Boat? Not quite

definitions.text: in the Blue Boat? Not quite

indicators.note: the piece for one's is written out two times in a row

parts.note: one is I, and 'one's' gives I plus S

explanation.surface: A question about a rower being in the Oxford Blue Boat, answered 'not quite'.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blue Boat is Oxford's top crew in the Boat Race against Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford's reserve crew bears this name, so its rowers are just short of the first-choice boat.

clue.text: Fair player has drink on board with Jeeves, for example

indicators.note: on board puts the drink inside the ship, so on signals containment here

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, which one is on board
port is a fortified wine
Jeeves, P G Wodehouse's valet, is a gentleman's man

explanation.surface: A fair-minded player drinks aboard ship with his butler.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeeves is the famous valet in P G Wodehouse's comic novels.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who plays fair and is a good loser is called a good one of these athletes.

clue.text: Objects about organ and arouses affection

indicators.note: the objects word goes round the organ, so about means surrounding

parts.note: ends are aims or objects
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a musical organ, yet it stirs warm feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks like the instrument but is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To make oneself loved or liked, a verb sense of winning fondness.

clue.text: Stone apparently found in county

indicators.note: the abbreviation is found inside the county word

parts.note: a shire is a county
app. is the dictionary abbreviation for apparently

explanation.surface: A gemstone is apparently discovered in some county.
explanation.definitionFit: This blue precious gem is a variety of corundum.

clue.text: Painting is put up for performers

parts.note: painting is art
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to set something is to put it

explanation.surface: A painting is hung up for the entertainers.
explanation.definitionFit: Professional entertainers such as singers or dancers, a stage word for performers.

clue.text: Landing area excellent on both sides

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI
R stands for right, one side
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A landing zone is praised as excellent all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both sides' gives two pieces: R (right) and PORT (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Planes land and take off at this terminal, so it is a landing place.

clue.text: The past not his traditional point of view

indicators.note: not says the word his is to be left out of the past

parts.note: history is the past

explanation.surface: A man's own past is not the traditional view of things.
explanation.definitionFit: The conservative outlook, named after the British Conservative Party's old name, values tradition.

clue.text: Those people's song lacks an intro

definitions.note: the people's has a possessive, but the defined word is the plain object pronoun; the 's links to the song

indicators.note: lacks tells us the song is missing its opening

parts.note: an anthem is a song
the opening two letters, an, are the intro to be dropped

explanation.surface: The group's song has no introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: The object pronoun for a group of people referred to elsewhere.

clue.text: Fantasy often preceding flight?

parts.note: a fugue (Latin for flight) often follows this free keyboard piece

explanation.surface: A daydream before a plane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is fugue, from Latin fuga; 'Fantasy' is a free-form musical composition.
explanation.definitionFit: A free, virtuosic keyboard work, often paired with a fugue, which is a fantasia-like piece.

clue.text: Violent fire damaged church

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of fire are broken and rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A violent blaze harmed a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferocious and savage, a close synonym of violent.

clue.text: Make provisional note of nice broadcast in Poland

indicators.note: the scattered letters go inside the country abbreviation

parts.note: PL is the international code for Poland

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of nice are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jot down a pleasant radio programme in Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: To pencil something in is to write it down provisionally, erasable later.

clue.text: Type of publicity in Telegraph initially

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity
taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Telegraph

explanation.surface: A kind of advertising carried in the Telegraph newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type of publicity' looks like the definition, but 'Type' alone is.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed characters are type, as in large or small lettering.

clue.text: Get round physical training in open

indicators.note: the get word goes round the training abbreviation

parts.note: to receive is to get
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Do a lap of PE in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: Being willing to accept new ideas is to be open-minded, a synonym.

clue.text: Safe flag

definitions.meaning: criminal slang for a strongbox that a safecracker opens
to tire or dwindle, as in '... out'; also the Blue ... signal flag

explanation.surface: A secure flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves' slang for a strongbox; also a verb for fading away, as in running out gradually.

clue.text: Small and cosy eventually

definitions.meaning: intimate and snug, a French borrowing for a comfortable small place
in due course, sooner or later, as two words

explanation.surface: A small cosy room, given time.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for intimate and cosy; split in two it is the phrase for sooner or later.

clue.text: Innards of Arctic bear cured of micro-organisms

indicators.note: cured means treated and changed, so the inner letters are rearranged
the innards are all but the outer letters of the two-word phrase

explanation.surface: A polar bear's insides are healed of germs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innards of' strips the A and R from ARCTICBEAR, leaving RCTICBEA, which 'cured' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective relates to germs, the tiny single-celled living things.

clue.text: German city's Eastern ascetic

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr, Germany

explanation.surface: A German city produces an Eastern holy hermit.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an ancient Jewish sect known for strict self-denial and communal life.

clue.text: Flower where atmosphere's black (in the underworld)

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the underworld word

parts.note: hell is the underworld
air is the atmosphere
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A flower grows where the air is dark, deep below in Hades.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a variant spelling of harebell.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of the harebell, a blue wildflower of the bellflower family.
